course-classifier.title: One update favors the observed label.
Opposite inputs require opposite class evidence.

course-autodiff.title: The squared input reaches the loss along more than one edge.
An empty objective has zero gradient.

course-tensor-views.title: A transpose changes the placement of the gradient.

course-optimizer.title: The first step includes decoupled weight decay.
Unequal microbatches are weighted by their counts.
No optimizer step means no decay.

course-convolution-backward.title: A single receptive field exposes both derivatives.
A point filter is a multiplication.
The center pixel receives overlapping contributions.

course-tiled-matmul.title: An identity product with balanced idealized costs.
Smaller tiles reload operands more often under this model.
A partial reduction tile still contributes.

course-loss-scaling.title: One overflowing step is skipped; the following step can recover.
A later bad microbatch invalidates the entire step.
Backoff can make the same gradient representable.

course-checkpoint-planner.title: The plan chooses a feasible persistent/replay tradeoff.
A tighter budget can require an interior checkpoint.
Uneven layers make equal spacing unreliable.

course-sharded-state.title: A zero learning rate preserves gathered parameters.
Empty owners remain part of the collective.
Empty shards require no optimizer storage.

course-byte-tokenizer.title: A frequent pair is merged before a pair of merged tokens.
The byte vocabulary handles unseen Unicode.
Training never invents a cross-document merge.

course-data-curation.title: Duplicates and evaluation contamination have different reasons.
Removing the held-out corpus changes only contamination filtering.
Duplicate suppression is not transitive through rejected records.

course-packed-evaluation.title: Uniform predictions have perplexity equal to vocabulary size.
An EOS-only document supplies no next-token target.
The partial final block contributes one target.
A logit shift does not change the score.

course-scaling-budget.title: Balanced model and data can beat a larger model at equal compute.
A budget can exclude every candidate.
A larger budget admits another regime.
A different data term changes the tradeoff.

course-policy-objective.title: A positive-advantage ratio can hit the clipping ceiling.
Reversing reward order reverses the learning signal.
Equal rewards supply no within-group signal.
Empty response masks contribute zero under this contract.

course-controlled-sweeps.title: The validation winner has worse test loss: do not change the selection rule after seeing it.
No exact-horizon records means no comparison.
An attractive early checkpoint is not eligible.
All candidates must share the comparison seeds.

course-loss-landscape.title: A step safe for one direction can be unstable for a sharper direction.
Changing only curvature changes the stability comparison.
The same noise is replayed for both recipes.
Momentum changes the trajectory without changing the loss function.

course-depth-signal.title: Measure depth with an unchanged residual bypass.
Remove only the bypass before comparing sensitivity.
Normalize the branch while keeping the bypass untouched.
A zero branch leaves an exact identity when residuals are enabled.

course-head-capacity.title: The two factors determine both expressivity and storage.
A tighter budget excludes one candidate.
The task distribution changes which head performs well.
No candidate fits a zero budget.

course-expert-capacity.title: The last token loses both assignments when capacity is exhausted.
More capacity preserves all routed mass.
Top-one ties can overload a single expert.
Zero capacity produces zero expert output.

course-generalization.title: Training and validation losses are measured separately.
Only the readout learns from fixed features.
Weight decay changes the update, not the reported data loss.
Changing only validation labels changes diagnostics, never final weights.

course-reward-audit.title: The proxy winner can fail the actual task.
A one-time pickup rule changes the incentive on the same traces.
Discounting changes the relative value of delayed rewards.
A per-step cost changes long-trajectory incentives.
